where: crates/blaze-cli/src/main.rs draw, print.rs finding, work.rs filed_answer, not_checked/waited.rs; crates/blaze-drive/src/request.rs Print::also, Request::base_of
what: tempo's check printed 30,017 errors, 29,283 of them `error[task-failed] .. needs X, which failed` from 8 roots, and 4,958 per-item `types-not-checked` notes; a no-op check spent 601 ms of its time printing them
cost: a lane's afternoon; two runner rounds were lost because the simulated home runs no build script for a workspace member, so the build-script fixture had no failure at all
cause: a waited task was filed as a TASK_FAILED error like a root, and every consequence finding was placed in its file (a read and an outline a file) before being drawn
whys: the filing reused one rule for a cause and its consequences; the drive dedups a crate's finding held by a library and its test unit into one print, so a waiter's cause can be a name that is never printed (the test unit's scope printed, the library's waited on)
class: a consequence counted as an error; a cause named by a name the printer dropped
prevention: done: WAITED (Cli 24) carries its cause's base name and crate in its words, never placed, grouped under its root; Print::also names the dropped copies; failures are counted apart from errors (Counts::failures); `--each` lists every consequence
annoyance: the runner's test filter is a substring list, so a filter that misses a test module admits a tree its tests were never run on; a build-script failure cannot be made in the sim without a registry dependency
workaround: the fixture's root is a source file that is not UTF-8 (a filed FileItems refusal) and a crate whose root cannot be read
